Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. GOVERNMENT ADVISORY ON BID CLARIFICATIONS The Finance Department is pleased to issue the following set of guidelines for all procuring entit ies to follow while asking for historical documents from bidders as clarification after the opening of bids. All procuring entities are hereby advised to follow the below set of guidelines, and all ad ministrative departments are asked to circulate this advisory among their subordinate offices. General Guidelines: Minor (Non-Material) Deviation: Means any deviation that does not materially alter or depar t from the characteristics, terms, conditions, and other requirements set out in the bidding docu ment. A minor or nonmaterial error or omission constitutes an oversight in the bidding docume nt that can be corrected without any changes in the substance of the bid. Handling Minor Non-Conformities: In case of minor non-conformities, the Bid Evaluation Commit tee shall seek information and documents with respect to those non-conformities which are hist orical in nature. Example: Missing pages/attachments, illegibility in a submitted document, non -submission of the requisite number of copies, or missing documents issued by an authority. Substantive Changes Prohibited: No substantive changes to qualification information or to a submission— including changes aimed at making an unqualified bidder qualified or an unrespon sive submission responsive— shall be sought, offered, or permitted under any circumstances. E xample: If a bidder has not submitted the Manufacturer's Authorization Letter (which is an eligib ility criterion) along with the bid, the same should NOT be requested as a minor deficiency to q ualify the bidder. Historical Documents Only: Shortfall information or documents should be sought ONLY in th e case of historical documents that pre-existed at the time of the tender opening and have not u ndergone changes since then. These should be called only based on the recommendations of th e Tender Committee. Examples: Audited Statement of Accounts, PAN Card, GST Registration Ce rtificate, Incorporation/Registration Certificate, etc. Related Shortfall Documents: Regarding qualification criteria, after the submission of the ten der, only related shortfall documents may be asked for and considered. Example: If the bidder h as submitted a supply/service order without its completion/performance certificate, the certifica te can be requested and considered. However, no NEW supply/service order may be requested to qualify the bidder. Deficiencies Apparent from Bid: The procuring entity can only seek documents and informat ion pertaining to a minor deficiency that is apparent from the bid already submitted. Example: If the bidder has not submitted the turnover certificate, it cannot be sought under Rule 23(15) of t he Assam Public Procurement Rules, 2020, as this cannot be interpreted as a minor deficiency. However, if the bidder submitted the turnover certificate but failed to submit the Audited State ment of Accounts, the statement can be sought. GOVERNMENT ADVISORY ON BID CLARIFICATIONS The Finance Department is pleased to issue the following set of guidelines for all procuring entit ies to follow while asking for historical documents from bidders as clarification after the opening of bids. All procuring entities are hereby advised to follow the below set of guidelines, and all ad ministrative departments are asked to circulate this advisory among their subordinate offices. General Guidelines: Minor (Non-Material) Deviation: Means any deviation that does not materially alter or depar t from the characteristics, terms, conditions, and other requirements set out in the bidding docu ment. A minor or nonmaterial error or omission constitutes an oversight in the bidding docume nt that can be corrected without any changes in the substance of the bid. Handling Minor Non-Conformities: In case of minor non-conformities, the Bid Evaluation Commit tee shall seek information and documents with respect to those non-conformities which are hist orical in nature. Example: Missing pages/attachments, illegibility in a submitted document, non -submission of the requisite number of copies, or missing documents issued by an authority. Substantive Changes Prohibited: No substantive changes to qualification information or to a submission— including changes aimed at making an unqualified bidder qualified or an unrespon sive submission responsive— shall be sought, offered, or permitted under any circumstances. E xample: If a bidder has not submitted the Manufacturer's Authorization Letter (which is an eligib ility criterion) along with the bid, the same should NOT be requested as a minor deficiency to q ualify the bidder. Historical Documents Only: Shortfall information or documents should be sought ONLY in th e case of historical documents that pre-existed at the time of the tender opening and have not u ndergone changes since then. These should be called only based on the recommendations of th e Tender Committee. Examples: Audited Statement of Accounts, PAN Card, GST Registration Ce rtificate, Incorporation/Registration Certificate, etc. Related Shortfall Documents: Regarding qualification criteria, after the submission of the ten der, only related shortfall documents may be asked for and considered. Example: If the bidder h as submitted a supply/service order without its completion/performance certificate, the certifica te can be requested and considered. However, no NEW supply/service order may be requested to qualify the bidder. Deficiencies Apparent from Bid: The procuring entity can only seek documents and informat ion pertaining to a minor deficiency that is apparent from the bid already submitted. Example: If the bidder has not submitted the turnover certificate, it cannot be sought under Rule 23(15) of t he Assam Public Procurement Rules, 2020, as this cannot be interpreted as a minor deficiency. However, if the bidder submitted the turnover certificate but failed to submit the Audited State ment of Accounts, the statement can be sought.
